title: Git Branching Strategies - Simply Explained

entities.name: GitHub
entities.quote: There are three big ones git flow, GitHub flow, and trunk based development

quotes.text: It's a shared agreement about who works where, how long a branch is allowed to live, and how changes get reviewed before they land in the main version.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines a branching strategy as a team agreement rather than a tool.

quotes.text: Never rebase a branch that other people are working on. Atlassian puts it as a single question to ask before every rebase, which is whether anyone else is looking at this branch.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the single most important rule of the episode.

quotes.text: A good way to start is to pick the lightest model that works. Then add ceremony only when something breaks.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a concise, practical recommendation for choosing a strategy.

quotes.text: The longer a branch stays alive, the more the rest of the project moves on without it, and the messier the merge gets when it finally comes back.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why short-lived branches reduce merge pain.

quotes.text: Copying a big company's setup without their testing and release process is tempting, and it rarely works because the model isn't the magic on its own. The practices around it are.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Warns that practices, not the branching model alone, drive success.

chapters.title: Pull requests and merge vs. rebase

takeaways: A branching strategy is a shared team agreement about how copies of the project get made and come back together.
Git flow fits versioned software, GitHub flow fits teams that deploy continuously, and trunk-based development fits teams with small changes and strong automated tests.
Merge preserves history while rebase tidies it, so rebase only private branches and never shared ones.
hook: When two people change the same file, someone has to decide which version is real. This episode explains Git flow, GitHub flow and trunk-based development for developers and teams new to branching. You will learn which model fits your team and which common mistakes to avoid.
